title: Version History
summary: Track updates and changes to the MedTech Europe Code App.

sections.title: September 2026 Update 4
sections.legalText:
Current

Can We Support This Event?

  • New tool: “Can we support this event?” checks what a company plans to provide against the Code: an Educational Grant, booth space or a satellite symposium, a speaker’s fee, an HCP’s attendance costs, a meal, an educational item, Demonstration Products, a donation and more. Open it from the Decision Trees page.
  • It asks only the questions that matter for your case, then gives the Code’s position (permitted, permitted if the conditions are met, not permitted, or needs a CVS decision or internal review) with the reasons, the conditions to confirm and the provisions it relies on.
  • For third-party Events it can find the Event in the Conference Vetting System (CVS) and use its current status. A Compliant decision covers the Event’s own venue, programme and social programme.
  • Each cost is assessed separately: registration, travel, accommodation, meals and fees.
  • Defined terms and references to the Code are links. On wide screens they open in the side panel.
  • After the answer, see other ways to support the same Event using the facts already given, and print a summary.

Conference Vetting System Check

  • The Conference Vetting System check, previously the decision tree “When are CVS assessments required?”, now has its own card on Home and its own place in the sidebar. For now it takes the place of “Can we support this event?”, which is on the Decision Trees page.
  • It now asks about the Event first: where it takes place, and whether you expect HCP Delegates from more than one country of the MedTech Europe Geographic Area. Then choose what the company plans to provide, from the types of support in Annex I, to see Annex I’s answer.
  • Where the support needs a positive CVS decision, find the Event in CVS below the answer. The answer turns green when CVS has assessed the Event as Compliant, turns red when the support cannot be provided (for example when the Event is Not Compliant), and stays yellow while the Event awaits a decision. What the status means is added to the answer. If the Event isn’t in CVS, the answer tells you to submit it or ask the organiser to.
  • For a national Event, you can check whether it has been submitted to CVS anyway. If it has, the answer turns yellow and asks you to clarify the audience with the organiser before committing to support.
  • New answers for Events held online only, which are not subject to CVS, and for audiences of local HCPs and HCPs from outside the Area, which Annex I does not classify.
  • For an Educational Grant that funds HCPs’ attendance at an Event outside the Area, the tree asks whether it funds HCPs from the Area (Annex I, footnote 3).

Corrections

  • Conference Vetting System check (previously “When are CVS assessments required?”): direct sponsorship of HCPs now gives the answer Annex I gives, “Not allowed”. It previously said a CVS decision was or was not required.
  • TPPT Checker: an agenda with a negative session duration now asks you to correct it instead of showing a result.

sections.title: September 2026 Update 3
sections.legalText:
Reading On Larger Screens

  • The sidebar and the side panel now sit against the edges of the window, and the text uses the space between them.
  • On laptops and desktops, drag the edge of the sidebar or the side panel to make it wider or narrower. Double-click the edge to go back to the default width. The app remembers your widths.
  • Text now uses more of the width. Under Line length in the reading settings (Aa), choose Narrow, Standard or Full. Full fills the space between the sidebar and the side panel.
  • The app now uses its intended typeface, Inter, on every device, including offline.
  • On very large monitors everything is slightly larger. Home, the chapter and decision-tree lists, the Knowledge Quiz, the TPPT Checker and Historical Declarations also use more of the screen.

Definitions And References

  • On wide screens a side panel beside the text lists the sections on the page and shows what you select, so the text stays in view. The text and the panel scroll separately.
  • Selecting a defined term shows its definition in the side panel instead of a pop-up. Close it with × or Esc.
  • References such as “Chapter 4” or “Section 3 of Chapter 4” in the Code and the Disclosure Guidelines are now links. On wide screens the side panel shows the referenced text in full; on smaller screens they open the referenced section.
  • On wide screens each search result has a preview button that shows it beside the text without leaving the page.
  • To hide the side panel and use pop-ups instead, turn the Side panel off in the reading settings (Aa).

Navigation And Layout

  • The sidebar shows full chapter names instead of cutting them off, and its search box uses the full width.
  • On tablets the sidebar opens from the menu button, as on phones, so the text uses the full width and every toolbar button fits on screen.
  • Home shows three sections per row on laptops and desktops, so more of them fit on the first screen, and the Code and Decision Trees pages show more cards per row on large screens.
  • The Knowledge Quiz lists chapters in a grid, with the number of questions and the Start button beside them.
  • In decision trees on wide screens, your answers are listed beside the question; select one to change it. A result’s Reference now opens the cited provision in place, with a link to it in the Code.
  • On wide screens the TPPT Checker shows the agenda and sessions on the left and the result on the right.

Speed

  • The app opens faster, and an installed app now reloads correctly when offline.

sections.title: September 2026 Update 2
sections.legalText:
Search

  • Rebuilt search. Results are now a ranked list of individual provisions, Q&As and glossary definitions, each showing where it sits, a short extract and the words it matched, instead of chapters with match counts.
  • Search understands everyday wording: plurals and other word forms, spelling mistakes, abbreviations such as HCP, and everyday words the Code does not use. For example, “doctor” also finds healthcare professionals, and “wife” finds the rules on guests.
  • When a word you type is not in the Code, the results say so and show the similar terms that were searched instead.
  • Put words in quotes to find an exact phrase, type a Q&A number such as “Q&A 31” to go straight to it, or type a defined term to see its definition first.
  • Filter results by type: provisions, Q&As or definitions. Summaries written for the app are listed separately from the Code text.
  • The words that matched are highlighted in the text, and search works the same way in the Disclosure Guidelines.
  • Search now understands a wider everyday vocabulary, for example “background check”, “going rate” and “raffle”.

Links And Navigation

  • Every official Q&A now has its own link, which opens the page with Q&As shown and scrolls to that Q&A.
  • Version History now has its own Website group in the sidebar, so it can be opened from every section.

sections.title: September 2026 Update 1
sections.legalText:
Glossary

  • All 38 defined terms now link to their definitions, including terms written with an abbreviation (such as HCP, HCO, CVS and FMV) and plural forms.
  • A term links the first time it appears in each section, and only where it is written as the Code writes it, so ordinary words stay plain text.
  • Definitions now show in full, and defined terms can be opened and closed with the keyboard.

Links

  • Direct links to chapters, Transparency pages, decision trees and the TPPT Checker now open the right page on a first visit, instead of the Home page.

Reading And Accessibility

  • Pinch-to-zoom works again on phones and tablets.
  • Reading settings (text size and spacing) are remembered between visits, and the settings panel closes with Escape or a click outside it.
  • Improved the colour contrast of teal text.

TPPT Checker

  • Fixed the exported assessment report, which printed the answer to the larger-event question under a question asking the opposite (“Stand-alone event?”). Reports exported before this fix may show that answer reversed.
  • If the TPPT Checker cannot load, for example when offline, it now asks you to reload instead of showing a blank page.

Knowledge Quiz

  • Fixed the answer check and cross icons, which did not show, and the results badge.

The Code

  • Corrected five small wording differences in Chapters 1–3 and Annexes VI and VII so the text matches the published Code.

sections.title: August 2026 Update
sections.legalText:
Historical Declarations

  • Added Historical Declarations to the Transparency section. Search past transparency declarations by company or beneficiary name, and filter by year, beneficiary country, company country, type and currency.
  • Open any declaration to see its full details: the amount and currency, the beneficiary, the declaring company and, where available, a description and a contact link.
  • Historical Declarations can be opened from the Transparency home page and from the sidebar.

Sharing

  • Links to the app shared in messaging apps and on social media now show a title, a description and the app logo.

sections.title: July 2026 Update 3
sections.legalText:
Transparency

  • Added the Transparency section, starting with the MedTech Europe Disclosure Guidelines (October 2025): the Preamble, Chapters 1–3 and Annexes I–III, with their Q&As.
  • Download the Annex I declaration CSV template, or preview it in the app. The preview is for reference only.
  • Search, bookmarks, Recently Viewed, citations, links and printing work in the Disclosure Guidelines as they do in the Code.
  • Defined terms in the Disclosure Guidelines and in official Q&As open the Code glossary definitions.

Reading

  • Combined each section’s Cite and Link buttons into one Cite/Link menu.
  • Recent searches are now saved only when you press Enter or open a result.
  • Q&A jump buttons are hidden while Q&As are switched off, and section buttons no longer overflow on small screens.

Accessibility

  • Improved keyboard use and screen reader support for the citation menu, copy actions, the Send a Suggestion dialog and the mobile menu button.
  • Decision tree filters now say when nothing matches.

sections.title: July 2026 Update 2
sections.legalText:
Search & Navigation

  • Added category breakdown badges (Title, Q&A, Text) to sidebar search results with tooltip hit counters.
  • Added interactive keyword filter search for the Decision Trees landing page.
  • Added recent search chips below the search box.

Citations & References

  • Added a multi-format citation menu offering Formal Citation (including access date and section title), Markdown Link, and Direct URL Link.
  • Added Copy Text, which copies a section’s text and Q&As as plain text for emails and memos.
  • Enhanced floating toast notifications for copy actions.

Reading Utilities

  • Added Q&A fast-jump badges next to section headings for direct scrolling to official guidance notes.
  • Added a sticky gradient reading progress indicator bar.

Feedback

  • Added Send a Suggestion to the header, which drafts an email to MedTech Europe, or copies your suggestion if no email app is available.

sections.title: July 2026 Update 1
sections.legalText:
Knowledge Quiz

  • Added a configurable Knowledge Quiz covering selected Code chapters, with randomized questions, results review, explanations, and shareable quiz links.

TPPT Checker

  • Added the TPPT Checker for importing PDF, Word, or pasted agenda text; reviewing detected sessions and session types; checking practical and hands-on duration thresholds; and exporting an assessment report.
  • Users remain responsible for reviewing the detected sessions and classifications before relying on an assessment.

Navigation

  • Added readable chapter and decision-tree URLs with browser Back and Forward navigation.
  • Existing Code section, decision-tree, Quiz, and TPPT links remain supported and are upgraded to the current URL format when opened.

Accessibility

  • Improved labels and keyboard access for TPPT agenda controls, session editing, dialogs, and mobile navigation.

sections.title: April 2026 Update
sections.legalText:
Multi-Section Architecture

  • Added the Home Hub with navigation to The Code and Decision Trees.
  • Added a section-aware sidebar and breadcrumbs.

Decision Trees

  • Added interactive decision trees, full-tree visualization, contextual help, navigation controls, outcome states, and links from related Code content.

Navigation And Reading

  • Added collapsible Code navigation, section deep links, previous and next chapter controls, and the desktop table of contents.
  • Added filtered Code search, match counts, search highlighting, glossary definitions, citation and link copying, print mode, and reader settings.

Bookmarks And History

  • Added browser-stored bookmarks for Code sections and Recently Viewed tracking for the last five visited Code chapters.

Offline And Keyboard Support

  • Added progressive web app installation, offline asset caching, and keyboard shortcuts for search and print.

sections.title: Initial Release
sections.legalText:
Initial Release
  • Initial release of the digital MedTech Europe Code.
  • Full text of the Code of Ethical Business Practice.
  • Initial implementation of accessibility menu.
  • Search functionality.
  • External link/sharing feature.
